meta.title: Operation of Rota Rod Apparatus in Pharmacology Laboratory

sections.purpose: To evaluate motor coordination impairment, neurotoxicity, and muscle relaxant properties of CNS-active drugs in rodents using a rotating rod on which the animal must maintain its balance.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacology laboratory for assessment of drug-induced ataxia, sedation, and muscle relaxant activity as part of CNS pharmacology and neuropharmacology experiments.
procedure: Inspect the rota rod apparatus before use: verify the rod rotates smoothly and the fall timer functions correctly.
Set the rod rotation speed to the protocol requirement: typically 10–20 RPM for mice; 5–15 RPM for rats.
Set the maximum test duration cut-off (180 seconds for mice; 120 seconds for rats) to prevent fatigue injury.
Pre-train animals for 3 consecutive days before the test day — select only animals that consistently remain on the rod for 3 minutes (cut-off time) as experimental subjects.
On test day, record baseline fall-off time before drug administration.
Administer the test compound or vehicle by the appropriate route.
At the specified time intervals post-administration, place the animal on the rotating rod.
Observe and record the time until the animal falls off the rod.
Allow the animal to rest for at least 10 minutes between consecutive measurements on the same animal.
Clean and disinfect the rod between animals with 70% ethanol.
Compare fall-off times: drug group vs. vehicle control group.
Calculate percentage impairment: [(Control time − Drug time) / Control time] × 100.
Determine ED₅₀ if dose-response data are collected.
Document all individual animal times, mean ± SEM, and statistical results in the data sheet.
precautions: Place padded cushioning below the apparatus to protect animals from fall injury.
Do not re-test animals that appear severely sedated or ataxic — this is endpoint for that time point.
Pre-train animals adequately — untrained animals show high variability and cannot demonstrate drug effects reliably.
Set a cut-off time and never force animals to continue beyond it.
Disinfect the rod between animals to remove odour cues.
Observe animals post-test for signs of excessive distress; return promptly to housing.
Follow CPCSEA and institutional IAEC-approved protocol.
